lastCompletedStory.title: Correct the raw-echo fixture to the real Ink collision shape

nextStoryContext: US-002 (CAM-364) was the last story in this PRD (2 stories total: US-001 replaced the discriminator in src/tmux/dispatch.ts, US-002 corrected the real-tmux fixture to match). raw-echo.ts's PROMPT constant is now '\u276F\u00A0' (production glyph + NBSP, still length 2, so the pre-existing char-wrap arithmetic and every AC6/AC7/AC8/2*paneWidth test is byte-for-byte unchanged -- verified green). The fixture gained an ADDITIVE word-wrap mode selected via a NEW argv[5] ('char' default | 'word'), never replacing char-wrap mode: computeRowsWord uses row capacity paneWidth-2*PROMPT.length (76 at width 80, vs char-wrap's paneWidth-PROMPT.length=78) and drops a LONE trailing space left over after filling a row to capacity, leaving only a PROMPT.length-wide indent on the next row -- which tmux capture-pane reports as blank (pure trailing whitespace stripped) while the real cursor still rests at column PROMPT.length, reproducing the measured real-Ink collision (blank cursor row, not the old char-wrap model's 2-real-character remnant). Two new real-tmux integration tests exercise this in test/integration/dispatch-geometry.test.ts (drop-mode correctly retries+push-undelivered; submit-mode still resolves in one send), using a payload of exactly paneWidth-2*2 'x' chars plus one trailing space (77 chars at width 80) -- the exact len=77 boundary from the issue's measured sweep. bootPane() now takes an optional second wrapMode param ('char' default) threaded into the fixture's argv. IMPORTANT SCOPING NOTE for any future story touching this fixture: the header documents the full measured 4-point trailing-space sweep (len=75/76 no-wrap, 77 collision, 78->x=5) verbatim as real production fact, but the fixture's own simplified capacity+indent model does NOT reproduce the len=78 point bit-exactly (my re-derivation, cross-checked independently against the issue's separate single-token sweep 77->x=3 and 153->x=3, gives a nearby-but-different value) -- this is called out explicitly in the header and is intentional (reviewer-judgment oracle, not an automated exact-match assertion); do not 'fix' this by gerrymandering a special case unless a NEW acceptance criterion requires bit-exact len=78 reproduction. dispatch.ts itself (US-001's discriminator) was NOT touched by this story -- no changes needed there, cursorRowStartsWithPrompt already correctly resolves both the char-wrap and word-wrap collision shapes since it only asks 'does the cursor row start with the prompt glyph', which is false for both blank AND non-prompt-prefixed rows.
